newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks skid lower at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks skid lower at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks broke out of a narrow range and slumped at the close Wednesday, halting their six-session rise on the heels of a Wall Street selloff, dealers said.

"It was a bit of the old saying, 'buy on the rumor, sell on the fact' today," one trader said, referring to news the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee left interest rates unchanged at the end of its two-day meeting Wednesday as was widely expected by the markets.
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV, which was virtually flat most of the day, closed off 1.2 percent at 699.24.
It had rallied 7.8 percent in the previous six sessions, climbing past 700 for the first time in three years.
"It's a bit worrisome that the 700 mark did not offer support today, although if we quickly reclaim it at the opening tomorrow the market may stay firm," the trader said.
Analysts were not fazed by Wall Street's sudden fall.

"Players are taking profits ahead of Friday's jobs report, which is normal because that's much harder to predict than the outcome of the FOMC," said analyst Hugo Daz Lourenco of C&E consultores. "However, local fundamentals remain very good and there shouldn't be a major correction here."
Lourenco said MerVal's near-term target was 728, where it capped a long upward march on January 16, 1994.
In the session the broad market index closed off 0.9 percent, with winners trailing losers 18 to 37 and 21 issues closing flat.
Floor volume eased to 25.1 million pesos from 28.8 million Tuesday, while over-the-counter turnover dwindled to 79 million pesos from 125.5 million Tuesday.
All main-tier stocks fell except power utility Central Costanera, which closed flat.
Heaviest MerVal losers were pulp and paper maker Celulosa, holding company Comercial del Plata and construction stock Polledo, which dived 4.1 percent, 3.5 percent and 2.9 percent, respectively.
